about.title: Grand Terrace Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Grand Terrace is a small community of about 12,464 people, and a sudden loss here is felt on nearly every block. In 2025, public records show 34 injury collisions in the city, 54 people hurt, and one traffic death. The heaviest collision counts fall along I-215, Barton Road, Mt Vernon Avenue, and the southbound lanes of Interstate 215. Behind that single fatality is a family now trying to make sense of what comes next. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, separate from any criminal case, and it exists so surviving family members can recover what the loss cost them: funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the love, companionship, and guidance that cannot be replaced. California limits who may bring the claim and generally allows two years from the date of death, with a shorter window when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Grand Terrace families with an independent attorney, for free, so you can focus on grieving while someone else handles the paperwork.

whyChoose.title: How LawProactive Helps Grand Terrace Families

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California gives standing first to a spouse or domestic partner and children, then to certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can explain where your family fits before any time is lost.

items.title: The deadline is watched for you
items.desc: A wrongful death claim generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the clock is shorter when a government entity such as Caltrans or the county may be responsible. Your attorney tracks that timeline from day one.

items.title: No cost to connect, no fee without a recovery
items.desc: Our service is free, and attorneys in the network work on contingency. If there is no recovery, you owe no attorney fee.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on I-215 near Barton Road. Is that a wrongful death case?
items.answer: It may be, if another driver, a company, or a public agency acted carelessly and that carelessness caused the death. Freeway collisions often involve multiple parties, from other motorists to trucking companies to the agency responsible for the roadway. An attorney can gather the CHP or Grand Terrace collision report and review what happened before you decide anything.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, not on your family's losses. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action that seeks funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of companionship and guidance. The two can proceed at the same time.

items.question: How long do we have to act in California?
items.answer: Generally two years from the date of death. If a city, county, or state agency may be at fault, a government claim must be filed much sooner, often within six months. Because those windows differ, it helps to speak with an attorney early even if you are not ready to make decisions.
